clue.text: Aunt Sally, perhaps — a legitimate target

definitions.meaning: Aunt Sally is a traditional throwing game played at fairs, so it is an example of a game at a fair
someone open to justified attack or criticism

explanation.walkthrough: Aunt Sally is an old British fairground and pub game in which sticks are thrown at a dummy's head; the phrase also means a target of easy criticism.
explanation.definitionFit: A person or thing it is acceptable to attack or mock is fair game, an idiom from hunting.

clue.text: Animosity resulting from false story about king

indicators.note: about means around, so the story goes round the king

parts.note: fiction is an invented, untrue story
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Bad feeling arising from a lie told about a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Conflict or disagreement between people, a clash of wills.

clue.text: Small sibling camping outside, demanding attention

indicators.note: outside says the camping phrase goes round the sibling

parts.note: camping means in a tent
sis is a short form of sister

explanation.surface: A little sister, camping out, keeps clamouring for notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'camping' looks like it describes the sibling, but it is the container, split as two words round the sister, which 'outside' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Persistent and pressing, refusing to let a demand drop.

clue.text: Woman given thanks after work unit is set up

indicators.note: after puts the thanks behind the reversed unit
set up in a down clue means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: the erg is a unit of work in physics
ta is British slang for thanks

explanation.surface: A woman thanked once the work unit has been set up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' reverses ERG into GRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name, as in the actress Garbo.

clue.text: Failure to go off and produce a report

definitions.text: Failure to go off and produce a report

parts.words: Failure to go off and produce a report
parts.note: a gun or charge that fails to fire and make its bang

explanation.walkthrough: 'report' here is the bang of a gun, not a written account.
explanation.definitionFit: When a gun or engine fails to fire as it should.

clue.text: Garment suitable for Burns Night?

parts.note: read literally, a jacket for a night when things burn: a jacket whose name suggests fire

explanation.walkthrough: Burns Night is the Scottish supper on 25 January honouring the poet Robert Burns; the clue reads 'burns' as setting things on fire, and this jacket's name sounds like flames.
explanation.definitionFit: A sports jacket, often with club colours, whose name also suggests a fierce fire.

clue.text: In East Berlin, oddly, it's raised and abandoned

indicators.note: In at the start says the next piece goes inside the jumbled letters
oddly signals the letters are put in a strange order
raised in a down clue means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: it is taken as written, the 's a link

explanation.surface: Something in East Berlin is strangely lifted and left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' rearranges E and BERLIN into LIBERNE; 'raised' turns IT into TI, which goes 'In' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A dissolute rake, one given to unrestrained pleasure.

clue.text: Until recently, an African republic's unknown river

parts.note: Z is a mathematical unknown
the Aire is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A former African state whose river is uncharted.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of the Democratic Republic of the Congo from 1971 to 1997.

clue.text: Reported severity of one fitting out sailing-ship

indicators.note: reported signals that a word is spoken out and heard

parts.note: rigour means strictness or severity

explanation.surface: A news report on how strict a ship's outfitter is.
explanation.definitionFit: A worker who fits a vessel with masts, sails and ropes.

clue.text: Woman in high-performance car is a flighty type

indicators.note: in places the woman inside the car abbreviation

parts.note: GT is gran turismo, a fast touring car
Anne is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman in a sports car is a fickle sort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flighty' means fickle in the surface but here a creature that flies: a seabird.
explanation.definitionFit: A large diving seabird, a creature of flight.

clue.text: Matter in dispute gets taken to court, almost

indicators.note: almost says the final letter of the phrase is dropped

parts.note: gets taken to court means is sued

explanation.surface: A contested matter ends up very nearly going to litigation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the D from IS SUED.
explanation.definitionFit: A point under argument is the topic in question, as in 'the point at stake'.

clue.text: Quiet and gentle riding, or walking unsteadily

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
an amble is a horse's easy gait, so ambling is gentle riding

explanation.surface: A choice between a relaxed horse ride and a stagger on foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving with a clumsy, shuffling, awkward gait.

clue.text: Islander volunteers directions without a lot of enthusiasm

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the directions go round the enthusiasm

parts.note: S and N are south and north, two compass directions
a mania is an excessive enthusiasm

explanation.surface: Volunteers are given instructions without much zeal, as told by someone from an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside: S and N enclose MANIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the Australian island state south of Victoria.

clue.text: Manorial steward once contributing to bizarre events

indicators.note: contributing to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An old estate official plays his part in some strange happenings.
explanation.definitionFit: In medieval England the overseer of a lord's estate and its serfs bore this title.

clue.text: Function originally organised by retiring Greek character

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word organised

parts.note: per means by, as in per post

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing backwards, so the Greek letter is read in reverse

parts.note: eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A role first set up by a Greek character who has now retired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' turns ETA into ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To function is to work or run, as a machine does.

clue.text: Frantically hides a gun, suffering mental torment

indicators.note: frantically means wildly, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: Someone madly concealing a firearm, in agony of mind.
explanation.definitionFit: In deep distress or anguish, tormented.

clue.text: Blunders involving old Cambridge examination

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the blunders surround the abbreviation

parts.note: trips are stumbles or blunders

explanation.surface: Mistakes in an exam at Cambridge in years gone by.
explanation.definitionFit: The honours degree examination at Cambridge University bears this name.

clue.text: Its two parts rhyme all right

definitions.text: Its two parts rhyme all right

parts.words: Its two parts rhyme all right
parts.note: an informal phrase for fine, made of two halves that rhyme

explanation.walkthrough: 'all right' is both the meaning and a nod to the rhyme working.
explanation.definitionFit: Colloquial agreement, meaning fine or OK.

clue.text: Overseer of royal forests revered dreadful king

indicators.note: dreadful signals that the letters of revered are mangled

parts.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A forest overseer honoured an awful monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dreadful' rearranges REVERED into VERDERE.
explanation.definitionFit: A judicial officer who kept order in the English royal hunting grounds, a post surviving in the New Forest.

clue.text: Socrates initially accepting time in disgrace

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the Greek letter holds the abbreviation

parts.note: Socrates was Greek, and his name in Greek begins with the letter sigma

explanation.surface: The philosopher at the start takes time over a matter of shame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' tempts you to take a plain S; instead it is the Greek name of that letter, SIGMA, Socrates' own initial.
explanation.definitionFit: A mark of shame or social discredit attached to someone.

clue.text: Continue to play with one in suit

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the phrase

parts.note: to act on is to go on acting or playing
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Carry on playing cards with one in the same suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' wants to be a suit of cards; it is a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal action is a lawsuit brought before a court.

clue.text: Go before pressure's on to surrender

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for pressure
re means on or concerning
to cede is to give up or surrender

explanation.surface: Advice to push ahead because pressure is on to give in.
explanation.definitionFit: To come earlier in order or time than something else.

clue.text: Pupil is rubbish, say, in gym

indicators.note: in says the rubbish and example go inside gym

parts.note: PE is physical education, gym lessons at school
rot is nonsense or rubbish
eg, for example, is what say means here

explanation.surface: A schoolchild is useless in gym class.
explanation.definitionFit: A person guided and promoted by a mentor.

clue.text: Players often practise these climbs

definitions.meaning: musicians run up and down note sequences as exercises
goes up, ascends a wall or slope

explanation.definitionFit: Musical exercises of ascending notes, and also ascending or clambering up.

clue.text: Flowering plants put on show in islands

indicators.note: in says the performance word goes inside the islands abbreviation

parts.note: CI stands for the Channel Islands
to act is to put on a show

explanation.surface: Blooms displayed on islands.
explanation.walkthrough: The Channel Islands are the British islands off Normandy, Jersey and Guernsey among them.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiny desert succulents, many of which produce showy blooms.

clue.text: Derrick managed to get into church

indicators.note: to get into says the running word goes inside the church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
ran means managed, as in ran a business

explanation.surface: Someone named Derrick managed to get into church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Derrick' looks like a man's name but is a lifting machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A derrick is a lifting machine with a jib, a type of hoist.

clue.text: Delivered by company, like Milton's engine?

indicators.note: by means beside, so one piece stands next to the other

parts.note: two's company, as the saying has it
handed means delivered or passed over

explanation.surface: Something brought by a firm, compared with an engine described by the poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Milton's poem Lycidas speaks of 'that two-handed engine at the door', a famously obscure weapon of judgment.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton's phrase describes the engine as wielded with both of a person's hands.

clue.text: A doctor's hesitation, in the light of warning

parts.note: MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A medic's pause in view of a caution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the light of' looks like 'considering'; the traffic signal is the meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The middle traffic signal, yellow-orange, cautions drivers to stop.

clue.text: See note containing swearwords causing disgust

indicators.note: containing says the musical note holds the swearwords

parts.note: lo is an old word for see or behold
oaths are curses or swearwords
me (also mi) is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A message full of bad language that revolts its reader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' looks like a written message but is the sol-fa note ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Repellent, odious, arousing strong revulsion.

clue.text: When he makes bloomers, his customers may scoff

definitions.text: When he makes bloomers, his customers may scoff

parts.words: When he makes bloomers, his customers may scoff
parts.note: bloomers suggests blunders that invite mockery, but they are long loaves which buyers eat up

explanation.walkthrough: A bloomer is a British crusty white loaf with slashed top; to scoff also means to eat greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman who bakes bread for sale, including loaves called bloomers.

clue.text: Second date broken by youth leader's girlfriend

indicators.note: broken means the letters of the word date are smashed and rearranged
leader means the first letter of the word youth

explanation.surface: A second outing interrupted by the head of a youth group's partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges DATE into TEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A regular boyfriend or girlfriend is called one's steady.

clue.text: Carrier possibly bitter about this perfidious type

indicators.note: about means around, so the drink goes round the carrier

parts.note: bitter is a kind of beer, hence possibly
a tray is used to carry things

explanation.surface: A carrier, perhaps a resentful one, regarding a treacherous person.
explanation.walkthrough: Bitter is a British hoppy draught ale.
explanation.definitionFit: A traitor, one who breaks faith with others.
